key_insight: Different transport paths can produce the exact same flow matching objective, yet dramatically change SGD variance and convergence speed; path choice is an optimization knob, not just a modeling detail.
engineering_relevance: For practical generative modeling, selecting a lower-variance path can reduce training cost and improve stability without changing the underlying FM problem.
method: Analyze SGD variance under different path families that share the same marginal distributions and velocity field.
Derive a tight iteration-complexity bound for linear velocity models with 1D Gaussian data and identify an optimal linear path.
Formulate PathOpt_θ to minimize variance under the same-flow constraint, then convert it into a sample-estimable constrained problem for numerical search.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the theory with experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets.
watch_item: Variance reduction must respect the constraint g_t ∈ G(p_t, v_t^*); ignoring it can lower variance locally but slow overall convergence.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
